name: StorageRemote
label: Cloud Storage
description: Connections to external storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, MEGA, S3, WebDAV/Nextcloud, SFTP, SMB) through rclone: backup copies and moving old files off the server disk.

fields.label: Name
fields.placeholder: Google Drive of the IT department
fields.description: How this storage is shown in lists and in the backup status.

fields.label: Storage type
fields.options:
Google Drive
Dropbox
OneDrive
MEGA
S3
WebDAV
SFTP
SMB
Server folder
Other
fields.description: S3 — Amazon, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze, Wasabi, MinIO and other S3-compatible storage. WebDAV — Nextcloud, ownCloud and the like. SMB — a Windows/NAS network share. Server folder — a mounted disk or NAS on this server. Other — any rclone backend (https://rclone.org/overview/).

fields.label: Root folder
fields.description: Everything is kept under this folder: backups/<site>/ and files/<site>/. For S3 — bucket/path (e.g. my-bucket/grunt); for SMB — share/path; for a server folder — an absolute path (/mnt/nas/grunt).

fields.label: Connected account
fields.description: Empty — not connected yet. Connect with one of the buttons below.

fields.label: Paste a token from rclone
fields.description: The simplest way, no app registration needed: on any computer with a browser install rclone and run the command shown in the dialog (e.g. rclone authorize "drive"), sign in, then paste the printed token here. Leave Client ID empty.

fields.label: Client ID
fields.description: Optional: your own OAuth app (Google Cloud console / Dropbox App Console / Microsoft Entra). Its redirect URI must be https://<your site>/api/v1/method/grunt.storage.cloud.oauth.callback

fields.label: Client secret
fields.description: A saved secret is not shown again — to change it, enter a new one.

fields.label: Sign in through the browser
fields.description: Needs your own Client ID and secret. Opens the provider's sign-in page and returns here.

fields.label: S3 provider
fields.options:
AWS
Cloudflare
Minio
Wasabi
DigitalOcean
Hetzner
Scaleway
Other

fields.label: Address (URL)
fields.description: WebDAV — the server URL (Nextcloud: https://<server>/remote.php/dav/files/<user>/). S3 — endpoint; empty for AWS.

fields.label: Port
fields.description: Empty — the standard one (SFTP 22, SMB 445).

fields.label: Secret access key
fields.description: A saved secret is not shown again — to change it, enter a new one.

fields.label: User
fields.description: MEGA — the account email.

fields.label: Password
fields.description: Nextcloud — better an app password (Settings → Security). A saved password is not shown again — to change it, enter a new one.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.description: Instead of a password: the PEM key (-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- …). Not shown again after saving.

fields.label: rclone backend
fields.description: Name from https://rclone.org/overview/ (pcloud, yandex, b2, box, koofr…).

fields.label: rclone options
fields.description: Extra backend options, one «key = value» per line; they override the generated ones. Option names — in the backend's page on rclone.org.

fields.label: Encrypt before sending
fields.description:
File contents are encrypted on the server (rclone crypt, XSalsa20-Poly1305) — the cloud keeps only ciphertext. Names stay readable.

Keep the password somewhere outside this system (or use «rclone config»): without it no backup can be restored, and the password itself lives in the database you will be restoring.

fields.label: Encryption password
fields.description: Changing it later makes everything already uploaded unreadable.

fields.label: Second password (salt)
fields.description: Optional, recommended. Same rules as the password.

fields.label: Test connection
fields.description: Creates the root folder, writes and deletes a small test file. Save your changes first.

fields.label: Show rclone config
fields.description: The same storage as an rclone.conf section — keep it outside the system to get backups back with plain rclone if the server is lost.
Every new backup set (System Settings → Backups) is uploaded to each storage with this option, right after it is made, into <root folder>/backups/<site>/.

fields.label: Copies to keep here
fields.description: Older sets in this storage are deleted after each upload; independent of how many are kept on the server.

fields.label: Backups in this storage
fields.description: Lists the sets in the storage; the chosen one is downloaded to the server and appears in Backups, ready for «grunt db restore».

Moves the contents of rarely used files off the server disk. The File record, previews and access rules stay; on the first request the file is fetched back into a local cache. Only one storage can hold files.

fields.label: Older than, days
fields.description: Files uploaded earlier than this are moved by the nightly job (04:00).

fields.label: Larger than, KB
fields.description: 0 — any size. Small files cost a request each and save little space.

fields.label: Public files too
fields.description: Website images are better kept on the server: they are read all the time.

fields.label: Only files of
fields.description: DocType names, one per line, whose attachments are moved. Empty — any file, including the library and personal files.

fields.label: Local cache, MB
fields.description: Files fetched back from the storage are kept on the server up to this size; the least recently used are dropped at night.

fields.label: Return all files to the server
fields.description: Downloads every file kept in this storage back to the server disk (check the free space first).
